annotations.description: Failed to block a 1/1 Rigging Runner with a 3/4 Thrashing Brontodon. The block would have prevented 1 damage with essentially zero risk - even if the opponent had a combat trick, the Brontodon's 4 toughness is too high to be killed by any reasonable 2-mana pump spell on a 1/1 first striker (a +2/+2 trick makes it 3/3 first strike, which still doesn't kill the 3/4). At 20 life the damage is negligible, but there's no reason not to block.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not block, taking 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block Rigging Runner with Thrashing Brontodon to prevent 1 damage at no risk.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Moment of Heroism on an unblocked Rigging Runner when the opponent had all lands tapped and no way to interact. This was a risk-free opportunity for +2 damage and +3 life (5-point life swing).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Moment of Heroism
annotations.betterLine: Cast Moment of Heroism on the unblocked Rigging Runner to deal 3 damage and gain 3 life, since the opponent had no untapped mana and couldn't respond.

annotations.description: Using Moment of Heroism on an unblocked 1/1 just for 2 extra damage and 3 life spends a card that could be much more impactful later — e.g., winning a combat trade, saving a creature from removal, or generating a 2-for-1. In Limited, combat tricks are most valuable when they change combat outcomes, not just for incremental damage on unblocked creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Moment of Heroism on unblocked Rigging Runner for 3 damage and 3 life
annotations.betterLine: Hold Moment of Heroism for a future combat where it can save a creature or win a trade. Just deal 1 damage with Rigging Runner this turn and preserve the card for higher-impact use.

annotations.description: Player timed out on Thriving Moor's color choice. The deck is B/G with Ghalta, Primal Hunger in hand requiring green mana. The default choice from timeout is almost certainly not Green, wasting the land's dual-color flexibility. With only 2 Forests on the battlefield and Ghalta requiring GG, an additional green source is very important.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out (no response) on Thriving Moor color choice, likely defaulting to White or another useless color.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Green to help cast Ghalta, Primal Hunger and other green spells in the deck.

annotations.description: Cast Celestial Enforcer (a 2/3 with an inactive tap ability since no flyers are controlled) instead of using Aerial Assault to destroy the opponent's tapped Thrashing Brontodon (3/4). The Brontodon is the biggest threat on board and is currently tapped - a condition that may not be available on future turns. The Enforcer is essentially a vanilla 2/3 without a flyer to enable its ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Celestial Enforcer as a 2/3 body with no active ability
annotations.betterLine: Cast Aerial Assault targeting the tapped Thrashing Brontodon to permanently remove the 3/4 threat while it's vulnerable. Could then play a Mountain and still have mana available, and deploy Celestial Enforcer on a future turn.

annotations.description: Llama4 Snark declined to block any of the three attackers (Thrashing Brontodon 3/4, Gorging Vulture 2/2, Suspicious Shambler 4/2), taking 9 damage and dropping to 6 life. Celestial Enforcer (2/3) could have blocked Gorging Vulture (killing it while surviving) or blocked Suspicious Shambler (trading). Either option saves significant life and removes an additional threat.
annotations.actionTaken: No blocks, taking 9 damage (going from 15 to 6 life).
annotations.betterLine: Block Gorging Vulture with Celestial Enforcer (Enforcer survives at 2/1, Vulture dies, take 7 going to 8 life), then post-combat Aerial Assault the tapped Suspicious Shambler. This removes two threats and preserves the Enforcer while staying at a safer life total. Alternatively, block Suspicious Shambler to trade and only take 5 damage (going to 10).

annotations.description: With 9 power of creatures on board, Ghalta costs only {1}{G}{G} (3 mana) and GPT52 has 3 untapped Forests. Casting Ghalta as a 12/12 trampler would set up guaranteed lethal next turn against an opponent at 6 life with only a 2/3 blocker. Ghalta tramples over Celestial Enforcer for 10 damage = lethal. Instead, they cast Pit Keeper, a 2/1 with no ability trigger (only 1 creature in graveyard, need 4).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pit Keeper, a vanilla 2/1 for 2 mana with no ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ghalta, Primal Hunger for {1}{G}{G} (reduced from 12 mana by 9 power on board). This creates a 12/12 trampler that represents lethal next turn through the opponent's only blocker.

annotations.description: Cast Keldon Raider before playing Mountain from hand. Playing the land first costs nothing and provides an additional mana source, potentially enabling more plays after Keldon Raider resolves (e.g., Goblin Oriflamme or holding up Aerial Assault mana). Always play lands before casting spells unless there's a specific reason not to.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Keldon Raider before playing the Mountain land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first, then cast Keldon Raider. With 6 mana available (3 Mountains, 2 Plains, Thriving Bluff), after spending 4 on Keldon Raider, you'd still have 2 mana open — potentially relevant for responses or if Keldon Raider's draw finds a cheap spell.

annotations.description: Discarded Mountain instead of Goblin Oriflamme to Keldon Raider's ETB. At 6 life facing Ghalta 12/12 and a massive opposing board, Goblin Oriflamme (an offensive enchantment giving +1/+0 to attackers) is nearly useless. Mountain at least provides additional mana to potentially cast multiple defensive spells in one turn (Aerial Assault + Dauntless Onslaught both cost 3 mana).
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Mountain to Keldon Raider's draw/discard ability
annotations.betterLine: Discard Goblin Oriflamme instead — it's the weakest card in hand given the desperate defensive situation, while the extra Mountain could help cast multiple spells in a critical turn.

annotations.description: Attacking with Celestial Enforcer into a board where Ghalta 12/12 (summoning sick but able to block) can eat it. Llama4 Snark is at 6 life facing lethal from Ghalta next turn. The only survivable line involves blocking Ghalta with both Celestial Enforcer and Keldon Raider while using Dauntless Onslaught to pump both (+2/+2 each), reducing trample damage to 2. Losing the Enforcer to a Ghalta block here is likely game-losing.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Celestial Enforcer into a board with an untapped Ghalta 12/12 that can block.
annotations.betterLine: Do not attack. Keep Celestial Enforcer back as a blocker. Play Plains, and plan to double-block Ghalta next turn with Enforcer and Keldon Raider using Dauntless Onslaught to survive the trample damage.

annotations.description: Failed to block the attacking Celestial Enforcer with Ghalta (12/12), which would have killed the 2/3 Enforcer for free with zero risk. The Enforcer is a relevant threat because it can tap Ghalta to prevent lethal attacks if the opponent ever gets a flying creature. Taking 2 damage for no reason.
annotations.actionTaken: No blockers assigned (timeout), taking 2 damage from Celestial Enforcer.
annotations.betterLine: Block Celestial Enforcer with Ghalta, Primal Hunger to kill it for free. No combat trick can threaten a 12/12, so this is completely risk-free removal of a potentially dangerous creature.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 6 life with no untapped blockers and only 1 untapped Mountain. While Ghalta alone is lethal, attacking with all creatures provides insurance against the small chance the opponent has a 1-mana instant that could somehow deal with Ghalta (unlikely but possible). There is zero downside to attacking with everything since the opponent has no untapped creatures to counterattack.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Ghalta, Primal Hunger (12/12 trample)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures to maximize damage redundancy and guarantee lethal even through potential interaction
